about: Something few residents know: Lunenburg spends less a student than almost every district in the state, and has for every year on record. Two more surprises behind it, then the reorganised site, where each one is a short page.

image.headline: What Lunenburg spends on each student
image.sub: {pp.facts[1].label.figures.n.text} Massachusetts school districts, ranked from the most spent a student to the least.

text: Lunenburg spends less on each student than almost any school district in Massachusetts.

In {pp.finding.figures.y.text} the town spent {pp.finding.figures.a.text} per student, counting every source of money. The state median was {pp.finding.figures.b.text}. Ranked from the most spent per student to the least, Lunenburg placed {pp.facts[4].value.text} districts, and it has been in the state's bottom quarter in {pp.facts[5].value.text} years the state publishes.
Two more you may not have heard:

🏠 The average single-family tax bill rose {tax.finding.figures.b.text} in ten years, while the tax rate fell {tax.finding.figures.r.text}. The bill went up because the average home's assessed value went from {tax.facts[4].value.text} to {tax.facts[1].value.text}.
🎒 On average, {g8.finding.figures.a.text} of Lunenburg's eighth graders don't come back to Lunenburg's schools for ninth grade. No other grade loses more than {g8.finding.figures.c.text}.

Each of these is one short page. We've broken the whole site up that way: {all|len} pages across {cats|len} subjects, each answering one question, each showing where its figures come from and what they don't prove. lburg.org/reports lists every subject at the top.
What's one thing about the town's money you've always wondered? Tell us in the comments and we'll point you to the page, or build it.
